reason: Spec Branch 0 (POWER): 9 of 15 folds are powered, below the pre-registered threshold of 10. The verdict is indeterminate and FR-019 forbids relaxing the threshold after the fact to obtain one.
retracted_first_pass: An initial implementation reported 'trackable' by applying the power test to candidate availability on the TRAIN window instead of to the selected configuration on TEST. Corrected; the verdict is indeterminate.
floor_defect_corrected: The first run reported 3/15 powered and, worse, a FALSE 'trackable' on n=3. Two separate defects, both mine: (1) the power test was applied to candidate availability on TRAIN instead of the selected config on TEST; (2) FR-012's floor was applied as an ABSOLUTE 25 to both windows, but train windows are anchored and 8.1x-23.4x longer, so it admitted configurations trading ~1.7 per 90 days. Rate-matching the floor took powered folds from 3 to 9. The adaptation was never the problem -- it was unconstrained.

adaptive_choice_concentration._note: 8 of 15 folds select the IDENTICAL configuration, and all 15 pick one of four. A per-fold optimum that is this concentrated is close to a constant, which is evidence for a fixed safe setting rather than for adaptivity.

early_late_drift: f00-f09 concentrate on atr 0.013 / adx 20 / rvol 1.9; f12-f14 shift to atr 0.02 / adx open / rvol 1.0. A real early/late difference (Principle II), but across only two regimes of the optimum, not fifteen.

two_state_test.indicator: mean atr_pct_roll over the fold's own TRAIN window, pooled across 11 pairs
two_state_test.degenerate_note: Both regimes select the IDENTICAL config, so the two-state scheme IS a constant. The indicator carries no config-selection information; HI/LO labels interleave rather than forming the early/late blocks the hindsight optimum suggested.
two_state_test.conclusion: Adaptivity fails at BOTH granularities on this grid: per-fold is indeterminate (9/15 powered vs a pre-registered 10) and two-state degenerates to a beaten constant. Fifth adaptive scheme to lose to a static value in this project.
